findings.message: Two T807 acceptance items conflict. Item 1 asks for the place's age plus d clamped to 17–35; item 2 asks for the same refill (id, name, birth year) a year older each season. In the seasons where the clamp applies (d ≤ −2 early in a cohort, d ≥ 1 late in one, about 10% of a refill's seasons), he stays 17 or 35 and his birth year moves by a year each season. Example: the owner buys a 19-year-old, d = −3, and the refill shows as 17 two seasons running. The unit test only checks place ages 21–30, so it skips those seasons. No fixed birth year can stay inside 17–35 for a whole cohort unless d is −1 or 0, so this needs a planning decision rather than a worker fix. Hand to the planner as an inbox item: allow ages above 35 (or under 17), narrow d near the ends of a cohort, or accept the moving birth year.

Under `SQUAD_SPREAD` `spread`, a refill takes strength − k + class + age term but neither the squad's re-centring shift (about +2, since the age term averages −2 over 18–35) nor the bench offset of −3. A refilled starter therefore sits about 2 lower than its place's level, also after the next summer when he plays 'at strength', and a bench refill sits about 1 higher. This matches the acceptance wording and `flat` is unaffected, but T808 should read refilled squads when it judges the gate, or pass `spreadLevels`' shift and bench offset to the refill.

The lane last merged si/rl10 at f70d1eda. baseCommit 8d70ca7a adds T804, which flips `UPGRADE_MEASURE` to `signed` and changes `staffSignings`' `joined` to `joinedThisWindow`. findings.message: Two T807 acceptance items conflict. Item 1 asks for the place's age plus d clamped to 17–35; item 2 asks for the same refill (id, name, birth year) a year older each season. In the seasons where the clamp applies (d ≤ −2 early in a cohort, d ≥ 1 late in one, about 10% of a refill's seasons), he stays 17 or 35 and his birth year moves by a year each season. Example: the owner buys a 19-year-old, d = −3, and the refill shows as 17 two seasons running. The unit test only checks place ages 21–30, so it skips those seasons. No fixed birth year can stay inside 17–35 for a whole cohort unless d is −1 or 0, so this needs a planning decision rather than a worker fix. Hand to the planner as an inbox item: allow ages above 35 (or under 17), narrow d near the ends of a cohort, or accept the moving birth year.

Under `SQUAD_SPREAD` `spread`, a refill takes strength − k + class + age term but neither the squad's re-centring shift (about +2, since the age term averages −2 over 18–35) nor the bench offset of −3. review.summary:
T813 (c3e45d26 against 9d33688e) meets its acceptance. The merge only brings in the base's spec/STATE.md and spec/work/rl10.json runtime state; every other change is inside the task's touches.

`scripts/find-goal-seeds.ts` builds each scene with the specs' own fixture helpers and readers: careerWorld, advanceToNextMatch, goalInstants, replayGoals and presentationSamples. For the archived scene it also uses archivePlayback, which is what RecordsRoom.tsx renders for openRecordedMatch.

- Opening scene: the script applies every pre-browser assertion from goal-replay and mobile-match-presentation. Those are: first highlight a home goal at 5′ or earlier, at least 3 highlights and goals, goals[0] at 1 : 0, and every pick with footage. It adds safe extras the browser steps depend on: all highlights are goals and each has a goal on the clock (the 360 cue count), a sample between the first two goals (the paused seek), the opening cue at least one clock minute after kick-off, and at least 15 s at 4x before the second goal (the clip's cue count).
- Archived scene: the script reproduces match-core's timing. Scores must run 1 : 0, 1 : 1, 1 : 2; the cue must name the first scorer; the first goal must come within 2 clock minutes and the second within 1 clock minute of the seek sample; and every goal must come before sample 80. It derives the seek sample as at−1, which with archive frames comes to minute−2. That matches the old literal 2 for the 4′ goal and the new 16 for the 18′ goal.
- `--check` reads each spec's single `seed:` value and match-core's minutes and seek sample, and sets exitCode 1 when a named seed or literal no longer fits.

The spec edits are literals and comments only: seeds goal-feedback-61 and goal-feedback-389, `[2, 18, 31]`, and `fill('16')`. The comments carry "found by scripts/find-goal-seeds.ts" with the new minutes. No assertion was loosened, skipped or deleted, and the remaining `goalWorld` user (the theme-tabs test) does not depend on the goal shape.

Evidence: I did not rerun the scan or `--check`, because the review checkout has no node_modules and must not be changed. I relied on the recorded worker runs (scan, `--check` exit 0 on the new seeds and exit 1 on the old ones, typecheck, lint, format, i18n, unit `--changed`, build). The coordinator's `--list` and its targeted Chromium run of the three files (13 passed, including the 5 gate failures) support the result. Approval does not rest on that run: the static match between the script's criteria and the specs' assertions is the basis.

Remaining findings are P3 only: a garbled result line, and `--check` being brittle in two places.

findings.message: The limits line is garbled and contradicts the checklist. It says "Worker's note:, so acceptance item 4 is unchecked: listing not run", yet item 4 is marked [v] and the verified line says the coordinator ran the listing. The verified line also mixes in commands the coordinator ran, while ARCH-30 says a task's verified line lists only commands the task itself ran and names in limits the specs left to the batch. Fix this when the coordinator closes T813: drop the stale sentence and move the coordinator's build, --list and targeted Chromium run into a clearly attributed note.

`named()` finds match-core's seek sample by searching for the comment text "Going back before" and then the next `scrubber.fill('N')`. If someone rewords that comment, `--check` reports "spec seeks to sample undefined" and fails. It fails safely rather than passing silently, but the cause will be confusing. Optional: anchor the match on code, for example the `fill('N')` that follows `scrubber.fill('80')`.

The opening bounds (latestMinute 5, goals 3) are copied into the script as constants instead of being read from the specs. If a later edit tightens the specs, for example to an opening goal at 4′ or earlier, `--check` would still pass on its own limits. Optional: note beside the spec literals that the script holds the same values, or have `named()` read them the way it already reads match-core's minutes.
